metadata.title: Patterns of teacher collaboration, professional development and teaching practices: A multiple correspondence analysis of TALIS 2018
metadata.venue: International Journal of Educational Research Open

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses TALIS 2018 lower-secondary teacher questionnaire data from participating OECD countries and applies a preprocessing step to handle missingness (excluding teachers with >10% missing values and imputing remaining missing values via a regularized iterative MCA approach in R). The manuscript does not report the use of TALIS complex survey weights (e.g., sampling/design weights) or any replicate-weight scheme, so student/sampling weights cannot be confirmed from the provided text. Because the analysis is an exploratory multiple correspondence analysis (MCA) rather than a predictive model, the paper does not describe weight-aware estimation procedures. Analysts using TALIS microdata should verify in the TALIS technical documentation whether weights are recommended for descriptive multivariate analyses and, if so, apply the appropriate TALIS teacher weights when reproducing results.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Secondary analysis of TALIS 2018 lower-secondary (ISCED 2) teacher-level data from participating OECD countries. Teachers from OECD partner countries not included in the analysis were excluded. To address missing values, teachers with more than 10% missing questionnaire values were excluded. For teachers with less than 10% missing values, missing entries were imputed using a regularized iterative MCA algorithm implemented via the missMDA package in R. The final analytic dataset contains 73,172 teachers.

main_findings.dataset_used: TALIS 2018 (Lower secondary, ISCED 2) teacher questionnaire (OECD countries)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Not reported (MCA: 2-dimensional solution; Dimension 1 explains 43.3% of total variance; adjusted eigenvalues; squared correlation ratio used for interpretation).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using TALIS 2018 (lower secondary, ISCED 2) teacher questionnaire the study leveraged teacher collaboration frequency, PD participation, feedback type, and classroom composition indicators to characterize teaching practices along MCA Dimension 1, finding that teachers who more frequently use clear instruction, cognitive activation, and everyday-life problem tasks are positioned opposite teachers who report less frequent use of these practices and collaborate less. This indicates that strengthening collaborative professional learning and feedback mechanisms may be associated with more cognitively activating and instructionally clear teaching practices, especially in contexts where teachers face student learning and behavioural challenges, though the MCA is exploratory and does not establish causal effects.

main_findings.dataset_used: TALIS 2018 (Lower secondary, ISCED 2) teacher questionnaire (OECD countries)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Not reported (MCA: Dimension 2 explains 22.7% of total variance; supplementary variables projected with deviation thresholds >0.5 indicating notable connections).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using TALIS 2018 (lower secondary, ISCED 2) teacher questionnaire the study leveraged disciplinary classroom management practices, teacher collaboration frequency, PD participation, and feedback source to characterize teaching practices along MCA Dimension 2, finding that frequent disciplinary management aligns with low participation in professional collaboration and PD activities, while occasional disciplinary management aligns with some PD activities such as teacher networks or observation visits. This indicates that school-level conditions enabling collaboration and PD (and ensuring feedback such as observations) may help shift teaching away from predominantly disciplinary routines toward a more balanced instructional repertoire, while the results remain descriptive patterns rather than causal estimates.

data.outcome_summary: This open-access study uses TALIS 2018 lower-secondary (ISCED 2) teacher questionnaire data from participating OECD countries (73,172 teachers) to explore how professional development participation, teacher collaboration, feedback, and classroom characteristics co-occur with teaching practices. The authors apply an exploratory multiple correspondence analysis (MCA) using FactoMineR in R, selecting a two-dimensional solution where Dimension 1 explains 43.3% and Dimension 2 explains 22.7% of total variance. The analysis shows that teachers who report more frequent clear instruction, cognitive activation, and everyday-life problem tasks are positioned differently from teachers who collaborate less and rely more on disciplinary classroom management. Supplementary projections indicate notable links between classroom composition (e.g., problem behaviour, refugees, socioeconomic disadvantage, low achievers) and these teaching-practice patterns, and feedback based on self-assessment versus observation is associated with different dimensions. Limitations include self-report measurement and an exploratory design without causal identification.
